ai.description: *Hemidactylus kangerensis* reaches 55 mm SVL. It is greyish-brown with dark dorsal crossbands and a pale venter. Key features include a flattened body, tuberculate scales, and a distinct tail base.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus kangerensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous dark brown lateral stripe running from the snout through the eye to the flank.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus kangerensis* inhabits the rocky outcrops and moist deciduous forests of the Kanger Valley in Chhattisgarh, typically found at elevations between 300 and 600 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kanger valley rock gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging after sunset to actively hunt insects on vertical rock surfaces and cave walls.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus kangerensis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus kangerensis* is endemic to the Kanger Valley National Park in Chhattisgarh, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at low to moderate elevations.
